topic: How can frequency planning address interference between satellite uplinks and broadband power line communication systems?
response: Frequency planning for satellite uplinks and broadband power line communication systems must employ techniques like channel separation, time division multiplexing (TDM), and frequency reuse to mitigate interference.  The required frequency bands for each system are defined by standards such as the ITU-R Recommendation F.104 for satellite communications.
reference_context: Satellite operators and manufacturers try to separate the frequency bands of the adjacent beams so that the interference is mitigated. Commonly for high throughput satellite (HTS) systems, the frequency band is divided into four subbands so that closer adjacent beams have disjoint frequency bands.
